notes: Uber and Careem are safe and cheap. You can't get taxi drivers to switch on the meter, so haggle. For Coptic Cairo, take Metro Line 1 (Mar Girgis). Giza is 1 hour away in traffic.
From June to September it is 38-42°C: visit the pyramids at 07:00, museums at midday and the Nile in the evening. Bring a hat and 3 litres of water.
Monument entrances take card only (2026), no cash. Book the GEM online with a timed ticket. Entering the Great Pyramid inside the Giza complex costs 1,500 EGP.
Koshary costs 50-80 EGP, ful and ta'meya 30, restaurants 300-600. Tipping (baksheesh) is expected everywhere: 20-50 EGP, or 10% in restaurants.
There are no 'free' photo or camel offers at the pyramids. Say 'la shukran' (no, thank you) and keep walking. Women should dress comfortably, with shoulders and knees covered.
In mosques, take off your shoes and women should cover their hair. Do not visit during Friday midday prayer.

stops.name: Giza Pyramids
stops.tips: Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure. Arrive at the 07:00 opening for cool, quiet conditions. Entering the Great Pyramid costs an extra 1,500 EGP (narrow tunnel). Haggle camel rides to 200-300 EGP. Card payment only.

stops.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
stops.tips: Included with the pyramid ticket. Approach from the Valley Temple, where the morning light hits the face.

stops.name: Panorama Point Giza
stops.tips: A desert viewpoint that takes in all three pyramids at once: the classic photo.

stops.name: Khufu's Restaurant Giza
stops.tips: Modern Egyptian cuisine with pyramid views. Book ahead; 9 Pyramids Lounge is an alternative.

stops.name: Giza Sound and Light Show
stops.tips: A sound and light show in front of the Sphinx. Nights are cool; buy tickets in advance.

backups.name: 9 Pyramids Lounge
backups.tips: Lunch in the desert with pyramid views. Go here if Khufu's is full.

backups.name: Giza Camel Ride
backups.tips: 30 minutes on a camel in the desert. Fix the price beforehand.

stops.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
stops.tips: The vast museum opened in 2025. It holds Tutankhamun's complete treasure (5,000 pieces) and Khufu's solar boat. Book a timed ticket online (~1,450 EGP), allow 3-4 hours and take a morning slot.

stops.name: GEM Food Court
stops.tips: The eating area inside the museum, with pyramid views.

stops.name: Grand Egyptian Museum Garden and Obelisk
stops.tips: The hanging obelisk and the outer courtyard. Good for photos with the pyramid skyline.

stops.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
stops.tips: Cairo's most famous koshary (rice, lentils and pasta) since the 1950s. Downtown, four floors, 80 EGP.

backups.name: Zooba Downtown
backups.tips: Modern Egyptian street food: ta'meya and hawawshi.

backups.name: Egyptian Museum Tahrir
backups.tips: The old museum, home to the mummies and artefacts not moved to the GEM.

stops.name: Citadel of Saladin and Muhammad Ali Mosque
stops.tips: A fortress and an alabaster mosque. The terrace has views over Cairo and the pyramids.

stops.name: Sultan Hassan Mosque
stops.tips: A Mamluk masterpiece with a huge courtyard and a sense of calm.

stops.name: Al-Muizz Street
stops.tips: A Fatimid street of mosques, sabils (public fountains) and the Beit el-Suhaymi house, lit up at night.

stops.name: Naguib Mahfouz Cafe
stops.tips: Run by Oberoi inside Khan el-Khalili. Try the molokhia (jute leaf stew) and mint tea; air-conditioned.

stops.name: Khan el-Khalili
stops.tips: A 14th-century bazaar selling copper, spices and papyrus. Haggle down to a third of the first price. El Fishawy cafe is open 24 hours.

backups.name: El Fishawy Cafe
backups.tips: A mirrored cafe since 1773: mint tea and shisha.

backups.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
backups.tips: A mosque-university since 970. Go here instead of Sultan Hassan.

stops.name: Hanging Church
stops.tips: A 3rd-century church built over a Roman fortress, in Coptic Cairo. Take the metro to Mar Girgis.

stops.name: Coptic Museum
stops.tips: Coptic art and the Nag Hammadi texts.

stops.name: Ben Ezra Synagogue
stops.tips: Said to be where Moses was found. Home of the Cairo Geniza.

stops.name: Abou El Sid Zamalek
stops.tips: Egyptian food in 1920s-style decor in Zamalek. Try the stuffed pigeon and molokhia.

stops.name: Nile Felucca Ride
stops.tips: A one-hour sail on a felucca from Zamalek at sunset. Agree the price per boat.

backups.name: Sequoia Zamalek
backups.tips: A terrace on the Nile with shisha and meze. Go here instead of the felucca.

backups.name: Cairo Tower
backups.tips: A 187 m tower in Zamalek with city views.

stops.name: Saqqara Step Pyramid
stops.tips: The world's oldest pyramid (Djoser). The Serapeum, with its underground bull sarcophagi, costs an extra ticket. Cooler in the morning.

stops.name: Dahshur Red Pyramid
stops.tips: Entry inside the Red Pyramid is included (steep tunnel). The Bent Pyramid is next door and there are few tourists.

stops.name: Memphis Open Air Museum
stops.tips: The ancient capital, with a colossal statue of Ramses II and an alabaster sphinx.

stops.name: Saqqara Country Club Lunch
stops.tips: A farm restaurant among palm trees. Grills and Egyptian bread.

stops.name: Saqqara Carpet School
stops.tips: A hand-woven carpet workshop. No pressure to buy; just watch.

backups.name: Abou Shakra Giza
backups.tips: A kebab classic, for the way back.

backups.name: Bent Pyramid Dahshur
backups.tips: Inside the Bent Pyramid. Go here instead of the Red Pyramid.

stops.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
stops.tips: 2.5 hours from Cairo by train. A modern library and museums in a disc-shaped building.

stops.name: Qaitbay Citadel
stops.tips: A 15th-century fortress on the site of the ancient lighthouse, with Mediterranean views.

stops.name: Fish Market Restaurant Alexandria
stops.tips: Fish on the Corniche. Choose from the counter and eat with Mediterranean views.

stops.name: Kom El Shoqafa Catacombs
stops.tips: Roman-era underground tombs, a blend of Egyptian and Greek styles.

stops.name: Alexandria Corniche
stops.tips: Walk the seafront boulevard and take the tram to Montaza. Return train at 18:00.

backups.name: Mohamed Ahmed Foul Alexandria
backups.tips: Alexandria's classic for ful and falafel.

backups.name: Pompey's Pillar
backups.tips: A Roman column. Go here instead of the catacombs.

stops.name: Gezira Island Zamalek Walk
stops.tips: The island neighbourhood: ivy-covered embassy streets and the Nile.

stops.name: Aisha Fahmy Palace
stops.tips: An art nouveau palace and gallery in Zamalek.

stops.name: Ovio Zamalek
stops.tips: Zamalek's breakfast and brunch cafe, for a farewell meal.

stops.name: Zamalek Nile Bank Last Tea
stops.tips: A last tea at a cafe with Nile views. The airport is 45 minutes away.

backups.name: Cairo Kitchen Zamalek
backups.tips: Home-style cooking. Go here instead of Ovio.

backups.name: Museum of Islamic Art Cairo
backups.tips: One of the world's best Islamic art collections. Go here instead of the Zamalek plans.
